label: Staying grounded in success
title: Bhagavad Gita on Success: 7 Verses to Stay Grounded
description: Seven verses for when things go well: the standard you set (3.21), the trap of pride (16.4) and staying the same in praise and blame (14.24). Sanskrit, plain English and one thing to try.
h1: Bhagavad Gita on success: 7 verses to stay grounded
subtitle: For the promotion, the win, the good run. Read one a day, or all seven while it's fresh.
intro: Good news brings its own tests. Krishna's answer is steadiness: the same mind in praise and blame, gold and stone (14.24). These verses start with what success changes, that people now copy you (3.21), and the pride that can creep in (16.4). Then they turn to humility (13.8), the best kind of doer (18.26) and treating everyone as equal (5.18). The last is from the Mahabharata, a king who rose to heaven and fell as a python.

days.heading: People are watching now
days.line: Whatever a respected person does, others copy. The standard you set is the one people follow.
days.forYou: Success gives you an audience. Your team, your juniors, your younger cousins all take cues from how you carry it. Krishna says the world follows the standard the best people set.
days.today: Think of one person who looks up to you. What do you want them to copy?

days.heading: Where pride creeps in
days.line: Show-off, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance: the marks of a nature heading the wrong way.
days.forYou: Krishna names these so you can spot them early in yourself: dambha (show), darpa (arrogance), abhimāna (conceit). They grow fastest in a good season.
days.today: Notice one moment today when you wanted to be seen more than you wanted to help.
days.note: Use it as a mirror for yourself. It was never meant as a label for others.

days.heading: Gold and stone
days.line: Even in pain and pleasure, at ease in yourself; earth, stone and gold the same; praise and blame alike.
days.forYou: Krishna's free person treats a lump of earth, a stone and gold the same, and takes praise and blame alike. Enjoy the win. Just keep your sense of who you are from rising and falling with it.
days.today: Accept today's compliment with a simple thank you, and move on.

days.heading: No need for status
days.line: No need for status, no pretence, no harm, patience, straightness, respect for teachers, purity, steadiness, self-control.
days.forYou: When Krishna lists what real knowledge looks like, the first word is amānitvam: not needing to be honoured. He puts it ahead of everything else on the list.
days.today: Thank one teacher or mentor who helped you get here.

days.heading: The best kind of doer
days.line: Free of clinging and boasting, full of resolve and enthusiasm, unchanged by success or failure: the best kind of doer.
days.forYou: Krishna's ideal worker is full of drive and enthusiasm, and still doesn't boast or cling. Success and failure leave them the same. Ambition and humility can sit in one person.
days.today: Set your next goal, and tell no one about it until it's done.

days.heading: Everyone gets the same respect
days.line: The wise see the same self in a scholar, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcast.
days.forYou: Krishna's wise person sees the same self in everyone, high or low. Treat people the same way after the win as before it, from the CEO to the security guard.
days.today: Learn the name of someone at work you've walked past for months.

days.heading: The king who became a python

story.title: Nahusha's fall
story.body: King Nahusha was so successful that he was made ruler of heaven. Drunk on it, he made sages carry his palanquin and kicked one to hurry him along. The sage cursed him, and he fell to earth as a giant python. Ages later he seized Bhima in the forest, and was freed only after Yudhishthira answered his questions about what makes a person good.
story.lesson: Success can blind anyone. Conduct is what makes a person good.

verse.sanskrit: सुप्रज्ञमपि चेच्छूरमृद्धिर्मोहयते नरम् । वर्तमानः सुखे सर्वो नावैतीति मतिर्मम ॥
verse.line: Success can blind even the wise and brave. In comfort, nobody notices it happening.

days.forYou: Nahusha's own warning is the honest one: nobody notices the change while it's happening. That's why good seasons are the time to check.
days.today: Ask someone close to you if success has changed you, and listen to the answer.

faq.q: What does the Bhagavad Gita say about success?
faq.a: Krishna asks for the same mind in success and failure (2.48, 18.26), and describes the free person as equal in praise and blame, treating gold and stone alike (14.24). He warns that others copy the standard successful people set (3.21).

faq.q: What does the Gita say about pride and humility?
faq.a: 16.4 lists show, arrogance and conceit as signs of a nature going the wrong way. 13.8 opens its list of true knowledge with amānitvam, not needing to be honoured.

faq.q: Which Gita verse helps you stay humble?
faq.a: 13.8 (amānitvam, freedom from the need for status) and 5.18 (seeing the same self in everyone) are the two most often quoted.
